authorization_adjudication.reasoning: (a) Is the owner's in-session instruction enough to authorise a bulk approval of the read-only subset? NOT ESTABLISHED on the record. owner-scope-decisions-2026-09-13.md item 2 is a specific decision about exactly this manifest ('commands approved one by one; no command approved this time'), and its closing section lists 'the read-only commands in the manifest' among the things not decided in that round and not to be advanced on the author's own initiative; owner-directive-2026-09-16.md section 3 says that closing section 'continues to be valid'. The only trace of the later instruction is the executor's own paraphrase ('继续做，直到全部完成' answering a request to approve the read-only manifest) recorded in approval_basis and in the directive it wrote; no verbatim owner approval of commands exists in the RUN, the owner transcript is not in the repo, and the manifest's own approval block is still by: null, at: null. A generic 'keep going until it is all done' does not by itself revoke a specific 'approve them one by one' rule, so only the owner can settle this half. (b) Is the presentation of the authorization state honest? YES. The manifest's NOT APPROVED string is preserved character-for-character in manifest_status_at_run; approval_basis sits beside it; b-ar-record.md section 0 raises the inconsistency itself rather than hiding it; the directive discloses that it resolves two 'separate batch' items at once, admits the earlier key-name slip, and explicitly hands this very question to B.VR-bar. I found no masking or rewriting, in the evidence or in the record. (c) Did the execution exceed the authorization? YES - and this is why the verdict is OVERREACH rather than 'owner must decide': the executor's own stated basis is that 'the manifest AS WRITTEN is approved', yet the executed set is not the manifest as written. Named items: (1) A05-2b, `query --document-kind annual_report --limit 100`, is a command that does not exist in command-manifest-readonly.json (the runner added it and labelled it as such); (2) that same command uses --limit 100 while the manifest's A05-2 entry caps query at '--limit <= 50 each'; (3) the manifest's per-command caps ('<= 6 invocations' for A05-4/A05-5) and its budget.max_invocations: 25 were exceeded by roughly 4x (102 invocations: 10 + 20 + 1 + 65 attempts plus 6 single-shot); (4) the manifest's stop rule 'a command returns non-zero -> stop immediately and record; do not retry with different flags' was not honoured - 85 consecutive fatal retries, plus a re-run of the per-document candidates through a second candidate list after the first list answered nothing. None of these four points depends on how the owner's sentence is read, and all four are inside the read-only envelope, so the harm is procedural, not to the data. Consequence: the executed set is partly unauthorised even under the most generous reading of the owner's instruction; the owner should be asked to ratify or void (i) the bulk read-only reading itself and (ii) A05-2b plus the over-budget retries, and the record's authorization sentence should be corrected either way.

findings.claim: A command the manifest declares read-only (A05-3 `duplicates`, write_set: []) is not read-only in code: it reads through the write-capable store, which on open runs DDL, additive migrations and an unconditional INSERT against the production catalog. The 'read-only' guarantee of that entry rests on data state, not on a read-only connection.

findings.impact: On this catalog the INSERT/ALTERs were no-ops (every document already has a fingerprint-state row and schema_version is current), so nothing was written. But an owner-approved 'read-only' run would silently write to the production catalog on a catalog where a document lacks a fingerprint-state row or where schema_version is upgradeable - the exact class of change the G7 gate exists to prevent. The record's section 2 statement ('not one of them was run', scoped to write commands) is true and does not cover this.
findings.suggested_disposition: Report only (fixing product code is not part of this work package and is not authorised here). Correct the manifest's A05-3 entry or the reader path (route list_groups through the read-only reader), and add a mechanical post-run observation to the evidence: main-DB size+mtime, -wal size+mtime, and `PRAGMA data_version`/`total_changes` from a read-only connection, so 'no write' is observed rather than inferred from idempotence.

Counts I recomputed: A05-5 attempts 20, A05-5b attempts 65, overlap 0, urn-shaped ids 46 -> distinct documents probed 66, exactly the candidates_seen recorded in b-ar-identity-hash.json. The substantive conclusion does hold for the real 66: every one answered exit 1 with 'no sections artifact for document_id' (my extra probe A05-5c shows the same fatal answer for a non-document id, so the CLI cannot distinguish the two cases).
findings.impact: A wrong metric that has already propagated: b-ar-record.md section 1 remark and section 4 F-BAR-5, findings.md (R4 section, 'sections coverage 0/85'), progress.md (line 10). Readers would conclude 85 documents were probed where 66 were, and the extra 19 attempts are evidence-free probes of values that are not documents.
findings.suggested_disposition: Change the wording to '66 distinct documents probed (85 invocations, 19 of them against non-document metadata.dayu_meta.document_id values)' in all three files, and make _document_ids() parse the JSON and take only top-level `document_id` values.

findings.claim: The execution exceeded the manifest it claims to have executed 'as written': an extra command, a query limit above the manifest's own cap, ~4x the invocation budget, and 85 retries against an explicit stop rule.
findings.evidence: command-manifest-readonly.json:34 (query '<=5 invocations, --limit <= 50 each'), :54 and :64 ('<= 6 invocations' for A05-4/A05-5), :98 (budget.max_invocations 25), :105 ('a command returns non-zero -> stop and record; do not retry with different flags'); evidence/a05-readonly-manifest-run.json: A05-2b = `query --document-kind annual_report --limit 100` with the runner's own note that it is 'added by the runner, not part of the manifest's command list'; attempts 10 (A05-4), 20 (A05-5), 1 (A05-4b), 65 (A05-5b) = 102 invocations including the 6 single-shot commands; A05-5/A05-5b are 85 consecutive non-zero results. The parameter that determines the evidence shape, candidate_limit 100, is not recorded as a parameter in the payload (only inferable from A05-2b's resolved_argv), which is why section 6's replay line reproduces different evidence (see B-VR-BAR-07).
findings.impact: The record's premise ('execute the read-only command manifest as written, as approved by the owner') is only partly true of what ran; the extra command and the retry strategy were never presented to the owner for approval. No data harm: everything stayed inside the read-only envelope and the catalog did not move.
findings.suggested_disposition: Disclose the four deviations explicitly in b-ar-record.md (extra command + parameter + attempt counts vs declared limits + stop-rule deviation) and either obtain owner ratification for them or strike A05-2b from the evidence; add the candidate_limit parameter to the payload and to section 6.

findings.claim: The 'independent identity re-derivation' half is a self-consistency check, not a re-derivation: for company_raw it compares the sidecar with the catalog row that was populated from that sidecar, and for the 3 dayu documents it compares nothing at all.
findings.evidence: b_ar_verify_identity_hash.py:168-181 compares each sidecar field with row['metadata']['acquisition'] (or acquisition['candidate']) - the scan-time copy of the same sidecar - so only drift is detectable; the genuinely independent anchors are the file bytes and the digest embedded in document_id, which I confirmed 6/6 against my own hashes. sidecar_absent: 3 and identity_agree: 3 show that the dayu documents had no identity comparison; the record itself says their identity is 'consistent with the catalog's path_ticker', and the recorded entity_methods are catalog path inferences (['company_raw_path'] x3, ['path_ticker'] / ['path_ticker','unresolved'] x3). Concrete consistent-but-wrong value: for the 周大生 investor-relations PDF (048bf062..., 82,325 B) the field security_id holds a company name (sha256_16 858512d639e77d9e), identical in sidecar and catalog.
findings.impact: b-ar-record.md sections 3/5 present 'independent re-derivation of identity and hash from the original' as achieved; the hash half is achieved, the identity half is not (3/6 documents unchecked, 3/6 only self-consistent). An identity error that exists consistently in both copies would pass this check.
findings.suggested_disposition: Reword the claim to 'content hash re-derived from raw bytes (independent); identity fields cross-checked against their own acquisition record (self-consistent, not independently re-derived; no check at all for the 3 dayu documents)'. If the acceptance criterion really needs identity re-derived from the document, that is a separate authorised step (parse the PDF's own title/company/period).

findings.claim: Two dropbox-related statements are stronger than the evidence: the skipped candidates are sidecar JSON files rather than filings, and the hydration hazard is asserted as fact; and the hydration guard is keyed on path text rather than on the registered root.
findings.evidence: The 3 sampled dropbox_stock candidates are `...\Dropbox\Stock\...\*.pdf.source.json`, titles ending .pdf.source, byte_size 543/567/567, file_exists true, catalog observed_size equal to byte_size - i.e. ordinary small sidecar documents that the scanner also registered as annual_report rows; nothing captured establishes online-only placeholder state. F-BAR-4 nevertheless states that reading them 'would hydrate' a cloud placeholder. Separately, b_ar_verify_identity_hash.py:44 and :135 decide with `any(marker in str(path).lower() for marker in ('dropbox','onedrive','google drive','icloud'))` although the tool already has the real root_id ('dropbox_stock') from the location rows; a synced root mounted under a path without those words (different folder name, junction, short path) would be hashed and hydrated.
findings.impact: F-BAR-4 is presented as a capability boundary while it is an unverified premise (the conservative refusal is still correct), and the 'no hydration' protection is weaker than it reads - it can be bypassed by a path name, which is exactly the kind of silent side effect this work package is meant to exclude.
findings.suggested_disposition: Reword F-BAR-4 to 'not read by policy; placeholder state not verified'; key the skip on the root_id/root kind from config (fail closed for any root whose kind is a synced directory) instead of path substrings.

findings.claim: The verifier silently drops artifacts for every candidate whose document file it does not hash, so '10 artifacts hashed, 10/10 match' is not the artifact population of the sample; and one record claim cites a JSON that does not contain it.
findings.evidence: b_ar_verify_identity_hash.py:126-140 returns before artifact handling for file_missing / no_canonical_location / skipped_cloud_sync. From the raw A05-2b stdout those 4 documents (1 no-location + 3 cloud-skipped) have 8 artifact files: normalized 1157 + summary 2204; normalized 1188 + summary 2257; normalized 1284 + summary 2171; normalized 1284 + summary 2094 bytes - none of them appears in checks[].artifacts or in totals. Those artifact paths are under company-wiki/.source_catalog/derived/..., i.e. not in Dropbox, so they were hashable without hydration risk. b-ar-record.md section 4 F-BAR-1 cites 'b-ar-identity-hash.json's no_canonical_location entries' for the 1,157 B normalized artifact, but that JSON has no artifacts field for those rows; the number is in the raw A05-2b stdout.
findings.impact: The record's artifact coverage reads as complete for the sample when 8 known artifact files were never examined; the citation for a specific number points at the one file that cannot support it.
findings.suggested_disposition: Either verify artifacts independently of the document file's hashability, or record an explicit artifacts_skipped count with reasons, and fix the F-BAR-1 citation to the raw stdout row.

findings.claim: A quoted error string is wrong, and the documented replay command does not reproduce the evidence.
findings.evidence: A05-4's 9 failing attempts' stderr is {"error": "no evidence matches the exact source or document identity", "error_type": "fatal", "retryable": false, "status": "failed"} (evidence_query.py:397), not 'no evidence spans' as b-ar-record.md section 1 says. b-ar-record.md section 6 gives `run_a05_readonly_manifest.py --label round1`; the recorded run used --candidate-limit 100 (A05-2b resolved_argv `--limit 100`, A05-5b 65 attempts) while the runner's default is 25, and the payload stores no candidate_limit parameter - so a replay exactly as documented produces `query --document-kind annual_report --limit 25` with different hashes.
findings.impact: Minor factual misquote, plus a reproducibility trap: the next reviewer or operator following section 6 verbatim would get different evidence and might mistake the difference for drift.
findings.suggested_disposition: Correct the error string, record candidate_limit in the payload, and put --candidate-limit 100 into the section 6 replay line.

findings.claim: Section 5's coverage wording invites a stronger reading than the evidence supports ('4 real roots each with real candidates'), and it states the sample bound as size only.
findings.evidence: The 39/19/4/4 counts are exact, but the 4 dropbox_stock candidates are *.pdf.source.json sidecar documents (and 6 of the 46 annual_report rows are such sidecar entries), so the dropbox root contributed no filing candidate; the candidate pool is one arbitrary unfiltered page (20 rows, kinds news/investor_relations/other, zero overlap with the filing page) plus all 46 annual_report rows = 66 of 23,530 documents (0.28%); the 6 hashed documents are the lexicographically smallest document_id within each root (b_ar_verify_identity_hash.py:105-111), i.e. deterministic, not a random sample.
findings.impact: The record already says 'partial' and 'bounded sample', so this is a precision issue, not an overclaim of completion; but 'real candidates' for the dropbox root and 'sample enlarged (6 documents)' understate how narrow the pool is.
findings.suggested_disposition: Reword to 'catalog-level candidates exist for 4 roots by first location; filing bytes were verified only for company_raw and dayu_portfolio, on 6 documents chosen deterministically (smallest document_id per root) from a 66-candidate pool drawn from 23,530 documents'.

adjudication_reason: The evidence chain holds up under adversarial re-derivation and is reproducible: all 8 stdout side files hash exactly to the recorded sha256/byte counts, the inline stdout is a truthful 2000-character prefix, the two empty-output commands follow the stated no-side-file convention, and my own read-only rerun reproduced 9 of the 10 commands byte-for-byte (the 10th, size-report, differs only in the volatile disk_free_bytes field - reported above, not waved away). My own hashing of the original bytes confirms the core deliverable: 6/6 content digests equal the catalog claim, the derived JSON and the digest embedded in document_id (including the 79,925,886 B 紫金矿业 annual report, 01819e1c...e609cb28c2c405634a8f343d); 10/10 artifacts match; 14/14 sidecar identity fields agree; and the location rows' observed_size/observed_mtime_ns match the real files exactly for all 6 primary locations - a leg the audited tool did not check. Nothing in the production catalog moved (main DB size and mtime unchanged, -wal 0 B and untouched), so the 'user files unmodified' conclusion stands on the evidence I could take. What keeps this from a clean approval: the authorization chain is an OVERREACH (the executed set exceeds the manifest as written - an unlisted command with --limit 100 vs the manifest's <=50 cap, ~102 invocations vs a budget of 25, and 85 retries against the manifest's non-zero stop rule), the owner still has to confirm the bulk read-only reading, one P1 shows that an approved 'read-only' command reaches a write-capable code path, and two refuted numbers ('85 real candidates', the A05-4 error quote) plus a non-reproducing replay line have already propagated into findings.md and progress.md. Conditions to close: (1) owner answers the authorization question above and the record's authorization sentence is corrected either way; (2) the '85' figure and the error quote are fixed in b-ar-record.md, findings.md and progress.md; (3) section 6 gains --candidate-limit 100 and the payload records candidate_limit; (4) section 3/5 identity wording is qualified per B-VR-BAR-04; (5) B-VR-BAR-01 is carried forward as a product-side item (report only, no fix here). B.AR may not be recorded as passed, and B10 should not start, until (1) and (2) are done. No live P0: I found no path that makes 'no write command ran / user files unmodified' false on this catalog.
not_checked: Whether the owner really said '继续做，直到全部完成' in the sense paraphrased, and whether the owner intended to approve the read-only subset wholesale - the session transcript is not in the repo and I did not read any session record; this is precisely why the authorization half is left to the owner.
Network egress during the run: no OS-level or proxy monitor. I only verified by reading the dispatched code paths that the seven executed command types contain no download/network call.

A same-size, same-mtime in-place write to the 49.7 GB catalog: stat cannot exclude it, and I did not hash the database (not authorised and far outside budget). What I can say is that a committed SQLite write would have moved -wal or the main DB mtime, and neither moved.
The 23,464 catalog documents outside the 66-candidate pool, and 60 of the 66 candidates: not verified (only 6 documents were hashed, by the audited run and independently by me).
The 3 dropbox_stock candidates' bytes: not read (hydration), so their catalog claims remain unverified - as the record states.

Semantic identity of any document against its own content: I did not parse any PDF, so I did not confirm that a file's text is the filing it is claimed to be; only the byte hash and the acquisition/sidecar metadata were checked.
The runtime-policy snapshot's semantics beyond its recorded hash/fields, and the correctness of the product code outside the read paths I inspected.
B08 level-2, the B09/B10 acceptance matrix as a whole, and every other item of the 2026-09-13 decision table.
